_meta.purpose: High-quality remediation guidance keyed by finding-type / CWE. ENRICHMENT ONLY: a scanner that already produced a finding may use this to populate or supplement its 'remediation' text. Pure prose - cannot create a finding and cannot change severity.
_meta.source: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series + vendor hardening guides
_meta.usage: load_json('remediation_text', {}).get(key) where key is a CWE id or a finding-type slug

CWE-22: Canonicalize and validate file paths against an allow-list of permitted directories; reject any input containing '..', null bytes, or absolute paths. Run the service with least-privilege filesystem permissions.
CWE-77: Avoid invoking shells. Use parameterized library APIs instead of string-built commands; if a command must be run, pass arguments as an array (never a shell string) and validate each argument against a strict allow-list.
CWE-78: Do not pass user input to OS commands. Use language-native APIs; where unavoidable, use argument arrays (execve-style) rather than shell strings and apply strict input validation and least privilege.
CWE-79: Context-aware output encoding (HTML, attribute, JS, URL) on all untrusted data; adopt a strict Content-Security-Policy; use framework auto-escaping and avoid innerHTML / dangerouslySetInnerHTML with untrusted input.
CWE-89: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for every database access. Apply least-privilege DB accounts and suppress detailed SQL error messages in production responses.
CWE-90: Escape LDAP special characters per RFC 4515 and use parameterized LDAP APIs; validate input against an allow-list and bind with least-privilege accounts.
CWE-91: Use a hardened XML/XPath parser, parameterize XPath queries, and validate input against a schema; never build queries by string concatenation of untrusted input.
CWE-94: Never evaluate untrusted input as code. Disable dynamic-evaluation features; for templating, use sandboxed/logic-less templates and pass data as bound context variables, not as template source.
CWE-113: Strip or reject CR (%0d) and LF (%0a) characters from any value placed into HTTP headers; rely on the framework's header API which rejects control characters rather than building headers manually.
CWE-200: Remove sensitive data from responses, error pages, and HTTP headers; classify data and apply need-to-know access controls; ensure verbose debug output is disabled in production.
CWE-209: Return generic error messages to clients and log details server-side only. Disable stack traces and debug pages in production (e.g. DEBUG=False, custom error handlers).
CWE-256: Never store passwords in plaintext. Hash with a memory-hard algorithm (Argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt) using a unique per-user salt; rotate and re-hash on algorithm upgrades.
CWE-285: Enforce server-side authorization on every request using a centralized policy (RBAC/ABAC); deny by default and verify the authenticated principal owns or may access the requested resource.
CWE-287: Enforce authentication on all non-public endpoints; use vetted authentication frameworks, support MFA, and protect against credential stuffing with rate limiting and lockout.
CWE-295: Enable full certificate validation: verify the chain, hostname, expiry, and revocation. Do not disable verification (verify=False / CERT_NONE) in production; pin to trusted CAs where feasible.
CWE-306: Add authentication and authorization checks to every critical function; never rely on obscurity of the URL/endpoint. Place admin and management functions behind authenticated, role-gated routes.
CWE-311: Encrypt sensitive data at rest and in transit using current standards (TLS 1.2+/1.3, AES-256-GCM). Identify all sensitive data flows and ensure none traverse an unencrypted channel.
CWE-312: Encrypt sensitive data before storing it; use a managed key store/HSM for key material and ensure backups, logs, and caches are not retaining cleartext copies.
CWE-319: Disable cleartext protocols (HTTP, Telnet, FTP, SNMPv1/2c) and require TLS. Enforce HSTS for web traffic and redirect all plaintext requests to the encrypted endpoint.
CWE-326: Use strong, current algorithms and key lengths (RSA >= 2048, ECDSA P-256+, AES-256); disable export/legacy cipher suites and weak protocol versions on all listeners.
CWE-327: Replace broken algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES, RC4) and protocols (SSLv2/3, TLS 1.0/1.1) with current standards; centralize crypto in a vetted library and review the cipher configuration regularly.
CWE-352: Use anti-CSRF tokens (synchronizer token or double-submit) on all state-changing requests, set cookies with SameSite=Lax/Strict, and verify Origin/Referer for sensitive actions.
CWE-359: Minimize collection and exposure of personal data, enforce access controls and audit logging, and apply data-protection requirements (consent, retention limits, encryption) to all PII flows.
CWE-384: Generate a fresh, random session identifier on every successful authentication and privilege change; invalidate the pre-login session and set Secure/HttpOnly cookie flags.
CWE-400: Apply rate limiting, request size limits, timeouts, and resource quotas; use connection/concurrency caps and circuit breakers so a single client cannot exhaust shared resources.
CWE-434: Validate uploaded files by content type and magic bytes against an allow-list, store them outside the web root with non-executable permissions, rename to random identifiers, and scan for malware.
CWE-444: Use HTTP/2 end-to-end or ensure front-end and back-end agree on request framing; reject ambiguous Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding combinations and keep the proxy/server stack patched.
CWE-502: Avoid deserializing untrusted data. If unavoidable, use a data-only format (JSON) with schema validation, enforce allow-lists of expected types, and never use native object deserializers on attacker input.
CWE-521: Enforce a strong password policy (length-first, breached-password checks per NIST 800-63B), offer MFA, and rate-limit authentication attempts to resist guessing.
CWE-522: Transmit credentials only over TLS, store them hashed (Argon2id/bcrypt), never log them, and rotate any credential suspected of exposure immediately.
CWE-601: Validate redirect targets against an allow-list of permitted destinations or use indirect mapping (server-side keys to URLs); never redirect to a raw user-supplied URL.
CWE-611: Disable external entity and DTD processing in the XML parser (e.g. FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, disallow-doctype-decl); use a hardened parser configuration for all XML input.
CWE-639: Enforce object-level authorization on every access: verify the authenticated user is permitted to act on the referenced object id; use unguessable identifiers as defense-in-depth, not as the control.
CWE-732: Apply least-privilege permissions to files, directories, and resources; remove world-writable/world-readable access on sensitive items and review default permissions on deployment.
CWE-776: Disable DTD processing and entity expansion in the XML parser, or cap entity expansion depth and total expanded size to prevent amplification denial of service.
CWE-798: Remove hard-coded credentials from source and config; load secrets from a secret manager or environment at runtime, rotate any exposed values, and add secret scanning to CI.
CWE-862: Add an explicit server-side authorization check to every protected resource and action; deny by default and centralize the policy so no endpoint is left unguarded.
CWE-863: Review authorization logic for flawed checks (role confusion, parameter trust, ordering bugs); test with least-privileged accounts and centralize the decision in a single policy engine.
CWE-915: Bind only an explicit allow-list of request fields to internal objects; never auto-bind the whole request body. Mark privilege/ownership fields as non-assignable from client input.
CWE-918: Validate and allow-list outbound request destinations; resolve and pin hostnames, block requests to internal/link-local ranges and cloud metadata IPs, and disable unused URL schemes.
CWE-942: Restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to a specific trusted allow-list (never reflect arbitrary origins or use '*' with credentials); validate the Origin header server-side.
CWE-1004: Set the HttpOnly attribute on all session and sensitive cookies so client-side script cannot read them; combine with Secure and SameSite.
CWE-1021: Set X-Frame-Options: DENY/SAMEORIGIN or a Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive to prevent the page from being framed by untrusted sites.
CWE-1275: Set an explicit SameSite attribute (Lax or Strict) on session cookies to reduce CSRF exposure; pair with anti-CSRF tokens for sensitive actions.
CWE-1395: Upgrade the affected component to a maintained, patched release. Track dependencies with an SBOM and SCA tooling, monitor advisories, and apply Subresource Integrity (SRI) for client-side libraries.
version_disclosure: Suppress version banners (nginx: server_tokens off; Apache: ServerTokens Prod / ServerSignature Off; remove X-Powered-By and X-AspNet-Version headers) to reduce targeted-exploit reconnaissance.
tls_weak: Disable SSLv3/TLS 1.0/1.1 and weak ciphers; require TLS 1.2+ with forward-secret AEAD suites, enable HSTS, and keep the TLS library patched.
default_credentials: Change all default and vendor-supplied credentials before exposure; enforce a strong password on first login and disable or remove unused default accounts.
missing_security_headers: Add the standard hardening headers: Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Strict-Transport-Security, and Referrer-Policy.
exposed_management_interface: Restrict management/admin interfaces to a trusted network or VPN, require authentication and MFA, and never expose them directly to the public internet.
